items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: my daughter Rachel, she was going at camp

ctx.x: Marlon played the piccolo trumpet solo in “The Rite of Spring” up there in Tanglewood when he was about twelve years old under Leonard Bernstein. So they was going, and my daughter Rachel, she was going at camp, she went to Tanglewood and Eastman and all of them. I wanted them to get a good grasp of the instrument, a good, well not classical grasp but I mean a good grasp of the instrument, how to play the instrument. See that’s another thing with jazz. A lot of people want to play jazz and that’s why it’s so…

that I practice jazz. Like it’s hard for me to practice sometimes because the reeds are so bad, sometimes I’m in a room fiddling with a reed for three or four hours and my wife says, “well didn’t you practice?” “No I haven’t practiced, I’ve been here trying to get a reed to work.” And it looks like the reeds are just terrible now. I don’t know if you are having any good luck with reeds.
